react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on tyrosine metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. MetaboAnalystR PSEA ranks KEGG:hsa00350 first (p=0.0006), RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks it FDR=1.61e-06 with fold-enrichment=335.7 (rank 14 of 15), and Mummichog m/z-direct ranking places "Tyrosine metabolism" at rank 1 (p=0.00126) with 9 of 10 pathway compounds matched including L-tyrosine, dopamine, tyramine, and dihydrobiopterin (7,8-dihydrobiopterin). The three shared driver metabolites — L-tyrosine (KEGG:C00082), dopamine (KEGG:C03758), and tyramine (KEGG:C00483) — appear consistently across every ORA hit. The parallel Mummichog hit at rank 2 for "Biopterin metabolism" (p=0.0116), capturing L-tyrosine and dihydrobiopterin (KEGG:C02953), indicates disrupted tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) cofactor synthesis or recycling. BH4 is the essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase and tyrosine hydroxylase; its perturbation explains why tyrosine accumulates while downstream catecholamine products are differentially abundant. SMPDB alkaptonuria (FDR=1.28e-06) hits the same three compounds and implicates homogentisic acid (KEGG:C00544), a direct downstream catabolite of tyrosine via p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate oxidase; elevated homogentisic acid is the biochemical hallmark of alkaptonuria. The strong SMPDB signals for dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency and MAO-A deficiency further underscore disturbed catecholamine biosynthesis. Losartan (KEGG:C07072) and uric acid (KEGG:C00366) drive the top RaMP hit "ADHD and autism pathways" (FDR=7.41e-09), suggesting that altered dopaminergic and purinergic tone may propagate to neurobehavioral readouts. Across all three paradigms, the biological story is one of coordinated disruption at the L-tyrosine→catecholamine axis with secondary BH4 cofactor insufficiency.
